SUMMARY: hairstyle a long loose waterfall braid with soft side-swept bangs; costume full plate armor from neck to feet with big rounded pauldrons and a short heraldic tabard — a solid knight's silhouette; design idea Interlocking graphite-block courses form the breastplate and skirt panels, with narrow ember-lit seams converging at a sealed white-stone threshold at the waist.; face an elegant, refined presence; expression resolute.

A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Fermium (페르뮴) itself — the sovereign of the Fermium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a youthful face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: an elegant, refined presence; porcelain-pale skin; oval face; almond-shaped eyes of natural size; amber eyes; straight brows of natural fullness; a straight nose with a slim bridge; medium-full lips of natural width.
Body and hair: slender-limbed yet full-busted with rounded hips and a narrow waist build; a long loose waterfall braid with soft side-swept bangs; glossy graphite-black hair with a warm ember-red glow banked deep inside, like coals kept alive overnight.
Expression: a firm, resolute look with calm, steady eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: fermium: element 100, the first to reach three digits, found together with her twin einsteinium in the fallout of the first hydrogen-bomb test in 1952, and named for the physicist who lit the first nuclear reactor, a pile of graphite blocks stacked in a squash court beneath the stands of a university sports field in the winter of 1942; she is the end of the road for building heavier elements by feeding neutrons to a reactor, because the next step splits apart almost at once, a wall no neutron can climb; her longest-lived form lasts only about a hundred days, and no one has ever gathered enough of her to see.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — FANTASY
Costume: a high-fantasy royal or warrior costume — plate pauldrons or a gorget, mail or scale over a long tabard or robe, a circlet or crown, a flowing cape; metal ornament and regalia built from the traits above, subtle magical glow along the patterns.
Silhouette: full plate armor from neck to feet with big rounded pauldrons and a short heraldic tabard — a solid knight's silhouette. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Design idea: Interlocking graphite-block courses form the breastplate and skirt panels, with narrow ember-lit seams converging at a sealed white-stone threshold at the waist.
Colours: banked-coal graphite black, warm ember red, hearth-glow honey, frost white.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: a prophesied kingdom that does not yet exist: the end of the road along which fire is passed from hand to hand, a hundredth gate at the top of a stair of a hundred steps, a holy hearth built of stacked black stone blocks inside a citadel of paladins who keep its embers, and beyond it a sheer white wall no flame has ever crossed.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Fm) and atomic number (100) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, corset, bustle, Victorian tailoring, modern material, machinery.
